column2: Men, with their fingers, bring forth Agni from the two fire-sticks, the praised one released from the hand, the far-seeing lord of the house.
Agni has awakened with the kindling of the people, like Dawn approaching like a cow; like branches shooting up, his rays spread toward heaven.

He is conquering, great, the winner of many; the unforgetful, destroyer of fortresses, with the wise; leading the songs through the forests, he inspires thought, bright-bearded like a warrior with armor.
One of your forms is bright, another worshipful; you are like heaven, with two differently formed days. You protect all wonders, O self-sustaining one; may your fair gift be here, O Pushan.
O Agni, bring to the one who calls on you the much-working Ida, the gift of cattle, forever; may we have a son, offspring and descendants; may your favor be with us.

The priest, born great and knowing the sky, sits in the abode of men in the turning of the waters; sustaining the strengths in the pressed soma, he gives treasures to the worshipper and guards the body.
Let the worshipper praise the praised sovereign, lord of the powerful, the one to be rejoiced in by the peoples; with the deeds of the strong Indra, let the praiser, praising, make known the door.
Jatavedas lies hidden in the two fire-sticks like a well-borne child in pregnant women; he is to be praised day by day by the wakeful, offering-bringing men — Agni.
From of old, O Agni, you crush the sorcerers; the demons do not conquer you in battles. Burn the flesh-eaters, the foolish ones; let the weapon of the divine not let them go.
O unconquerable Agni, bring us the most mighty splendor; give us the path to abundant wealth and strength.
If the mortal hero were to follow, let him kindle Agni; having poured the offering continuously, let him enjoy the divine protection.
Your smoke rises brilliant; in heaven you are spread out, bright; for like the sun you shine by your radiance, O purifier, by your grace.
For you, Agni, bestow dwelling-given glory; like Mitra you are the lord. O all-seeing Vasu, you nourish us as with abundance.
Morning Agni, beloved of many, is praised like a guest — in whom, the immortal, all mortals kindle the offering.
Sing aloud to Agni what is best to carry; O shining one, wealth rises from you like a queen; strengths arise from you.
Desiring strength, I praise Agni, the beloved guest of every clan, your door-guard, with the thoughts of the strong.
Sing a vast strength to the shining god Agni, whom mortals have set in front like a friend for praise.
We have approached Agni Manava, the best slayer of Vritra, eldest, who is kindled with his high flame, O Shrutarvan, in the Arkshya.
Born by the highest law, when you were with the fellow-growers; when Agni was the father of Kashyapa, Faith the mother, Manu the seer.
We take hold of Soma the king, Varuna, Agni, Aditya, Vishnu, Surya, and Brahma with Brihaspati.
From here these have risen up; they ascended the back of heaven; like victors, they went by the path to heaven — the Angirases.
O Agni, for wealth and for the great gift we kindle you; praise the bull, great — heaven and earth for the offering.
When the priest declared that the prayer is Brahman, it was held; it encompassed all poetic wisdom, like a rim around a wheel.
O Agni, with fury answer fury; crush on all sides the strength of the sorcerer-demon, and cast down his power.
You, Agni, here worship the Vasus, Rudras and Adityas — the people who perform good sacrifice, born of Manu, dripping ghee.
I, the giver, speak much of you, O Agni; I am yours indeed; as in the refuge of a driver, in the great one.
Bring to the priest, to Agni, an ancient, mighty word, to him who bears the lights of the wise, like an ordainer.
O Agni, lord of strength with cattle, son of might, give us, O Jatavedas, great fame.
O Agni, best of sacrificers, at the sacrifice worship the gods for the one who seeks the gods; the joyful priest shines forth, thrusting away enemies.
Born from the seven mothers, they sought wisdom for glory; this firm one has been known among the riches.
And may that thought of ours, Aditi, come by day with help; may she bring happiness and comfort and drive away enemies.
Praise the one who is to be met, and worship Jatavedas, the wandering smoke, with unseized flame.
No mortal enemy rules over him by deceit — he who has given to Agni, the receiver of offerings.
O Agni, lord of the good, drive far away this crooked foe and thief, hard to restrain; make the way easy for us.
Hear, O Agni, my new hymn, O hero, lord of the people; burn down with heat the deceitful demons.
Sing to the greatest, to Agni, keeper of truth, mighty, with bright flame, praised from near.
That man crosses over, O Agni, with your helps and heroic deeds of strength — he whose friendship you have favored.
Praise him, the sun-leader, the god; the gods have set him as the unfailing god; you carry the offering among the gods.
Do not be angry at us, the guest — this Agni, the Vasu, much praised, who is a good priest of the good sacrifice.
Auspicious for us is Agni to whom the offering is poured; auspicious is the gift, O fortunate one; auspicious the sacrifice, and auspicious the praises.
We choose you, best of sacrificers, god, among the gods, the immortal priest, skilful in this sacrifice.
O Agni, bring that splendor which overcomes whatever devourer there is in the house, the anger of men hard to resist.
When the lord of the people, sharpened and well pleased, comes for the clan of Manu, Agni drives off all demons.
Sing to him together at the pressing, to the much-invoked, the mighty, for the blessing, like a cow for the powerful.
O Indra of a hundred powers, may the most splendid exhilaration of yours now, by that, exhilarate us now in the joy.
Speak to the cows in the pit, to the giver of the great sacrifice's song; both ears are golden.
Sing enough for the horse, sufficient for the cow, to Shrutakaksha; sufficient for the abode of Indra.
We strengthen that Indra for the slaying of the great Vritra; may he be the bull, the bull.
You, Indra, are born of strength, of might and power; being a bull, you are indeed the bull.
The sacrifice made Indra grow when he turned the earth round, making a cover in heaven.
If I were as you are, Indra, alone ruling over wealth, my praiser would be a friend with cattle.
Run, pressers, to each praiseworthy one for exhilaration; press Soma for the hero, the brave.
Drink this pressed juice, O Vasu, with a full belly; fearless one, may we be yours.
You rise up, O Sun, toward the famed bounteous bull, the man of good works, the archer.
Whatever today, O Vritra-slayer, you have risen upon, O Sun — all that, O Indra, is in your power.
Who led Turvasha and Yadu from afar with good guidance — that Indra is our youthful friend.
O Indra, let no quarters of the sky constrain us at night; with you as ally we would win that.
Come, Indra, bring for our protection the greatest wealth — victorious, ever-conquering.
We call on Indra in the great contest, on Indra in the small; the ally in battles against Vritras, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Indra drank the pressed soma of Kadru for the thousand-armed; there he took manly strength.
We, longing for you, Indra, cry loudly to you, O bull; know us, O Vasu, in this matter.
Those who kindle Agni and constantly spread the grass — to them Indra is the youthful friend.
Break all enemies; drive away the oppressors, crush the foes; then bring the desired wealth.
Here, as it were, I hear the whip in their hands when they speak; they adorn the wondrous journey.
These soma-offering friends behold you, Indra, like well-fed cattle.
At his wrath the peoples bow, all the tribes, as rivers bow to the ocean.
We choose the great protection of the gods alone; for our help, that of the bountiful ones.
O Brahmanaspati, make the soma-sounds ring for Kakshivan, the son of Ushij.
May he of attentive mind be ours, the Vritra-slayer, receiver of many libations; may the mighty one hear our prayer.
Today, O god Savitar, bring us good fortune with offspring; drive away the bad dream.
Where is his young bull with a strong neck, unbowed? Which priest worships him?
In the folds of the mountains and at the confluence of rivers, the sage was born through thought.
The singer, with songs, praises Indra, new sovereign of the peoples, the hero, conqueror of men, the greatest.
From the one with the fine jaw, the skilled, the generous one — Indra of the moon-drops, mixed with barley.
These songs of ours, O rich in wealth, have cried out to you, like cows to their calf.
Here they perceived the secret name of the cow, of Tvashtar, thus in the house of the moon.
When Indra led the great waters, the most manly, there Pushan was our companion.
The cow nurses, eager for fame, the mother of the Maruts and of the bounteous, the yoked bearer of chariots.
Come to us with your bay horses to the pressed soma, lord of exhilarations; come to us with your bay horses to the pressed soma.
The offerings, desired, have been poured to Indra as they increase him at the sacrifice, toward the final bath with might.
